owners: CSGRS public planar operations and homogeneous matrix admission
qualification.domain: Nonsingular affine restriction to z=0 with constant nonzero homogeneous weight and image in the XY plane. Normalize six XY coefficients by the weight, including negative weights; the third column is irrelevant. Native Hypercurve owns determinant and topology. Perspective/out-of-plane maps are Unsupported, zero weight with nonzero coordinate image is Unbounded, and an all-zero homogeneous image is Invalid. Unproved constraints are Undecided or explicitly qualified under the selected approximate policy. Invalid arguments are checked on canonical empty inputs too.
qualification.migration: curve transformed/translated/rotated/scaled now return Result<CurveRegion2, ValidationError>; try_ and context variants preserve the same native causes. contains_xy returns Result<Option<bool>, ValidationError>, with None reserved for boundary. Scalar adapters preserve all three input components and apply X/Y/Z rotations in order. Nonzero Z translation and out-of-plane rotations are rejected; plane-preserving half-turns perform reflections. Gerber, Hypercircuit, FFI and WASM retain typed causes. FabricationPackageError adds Construction and retains PartialEq without Eq.
semantic_evidence: Unchanged baseline regressions reproduce fourteen defects (3 pass/14 fail). Twenty final regressions pass, with independent exact coordinate substitution, area 18, volume 36, a separate manifold check, holes, affine-cut commutation, empty-result composition and mutation/recovery.

Matrix admission consumes the selected policy and preserves qualification through native identity shortcuts. Strict/approximate/strict does not promote approximate evidence. Definite membership distinguishes inside, outside and boundary from a native undecided blocker.

Hypercircuit translates/scales/rotates through its selected materialization context and aggregates certainty. Qualified empty construction remains qualified through subsequent transforms. Failures cannot become empty fabrication images.

Actual C, C++, Python, Go and generated Node/WASM consumers exercise errors, normalized coordinates, plane-preserving reflections, canonical empty operands and recovery. TypeScript checks the generated declarations.

cost_probe.kind: focused matched successful-output probe, not a supported-corpus speedup claim
cost_probe.claim: Same completed strict workloads include construction, operation, independent exact coordinates/area, output materialization, serialization and drop. All exact rows and paired checksums agree. Every favorable and unfavorable sample is retained. Warm adapter translation median is 15.2% higher and warm affine-matrix median is 15.1% higher; other latencies are mixed. Adapter rotation adds 15 allocations and 792 requested bytes per operation; other measured allocation counts match. Shared unpinned host and allocator instrumentation limit timing claims. Warm and varied inputs are distinct; varied does not imply globally cold scalar caches. cost-v1 produced no timings after its dependency mismatch; cost-build-v1 uses the exact baseline example command for cost-v2.

qualification.resources: No internal total-work, expression-growth, heap-byte or cancellation bound is claimed. Serial offline trials with two Cargo jobs use external 1800-second wall and 8-GiB per-process address-space containment; Node/WASM retains only wall containment because of virtual reservations. Allocation probes cover the Rust global allocator, not all native allocations or RSS. Identical non-executable compiler files in terminal trials are hard-linked with every path and byte retained; new trials copy to independent inodes.
